practices.statement: A short block above the description is read by scanning, so each line has to carry one fact on its own.
practices.quote: People rarely read Web pages word by word; instead, they scan the page, picking out individual words and sentences.

practices.statement: Lines that state a fact are preferred to lines that praise the product.
practices.quote: Web users are busy: they want to get the straight facts.

practices.statement: Where this block is stored is a shop setting, not something a page reveals, so the write target has to be confirmed inside the shop before anything is written.
practices.quote: Metafield definitions are schemas that specify the structure, type, and rules for metafields.

editorial.statement: Three lines per page, which is the lower end of what the comparable pages show, so nothing has to be stretched to fill a slot.
One fact per line: who the product is for, what it contains, what the child practises.
No claim about sales rank, awards or savings, even where a comparable page makes one: those depend on figures that a product page does not carry.
No detail that belongs to another market. Where a description explains a product through the school system of another country, that detail is left out rather than translated.
Nothing is added from what a product of this kind usually has. A line exists only where the page already carries the fact.
